raw_text:
Thanks — below is a 12-week progressive general-fitness programme tailored for a 58‑year‑old male, six months post‑MI, cleared for moderate‑intensity exercise only. It keeps exercise intensity at or below ~70% age‑predicted HRmax (approx. 115 bpm), avoids Valsalva (cue breathing), and excludes maximal lifts. The plan assumes full gym access and that you will monitor HR (chest strap or reliable wrist HR monitor) and perceived exertion (RPE 11–13 on the Borg 6–20 scale; “somewhat hard”). Stop/modify if any cardiac symptoms (chest pain, undue breathlessness, lightheadedness, palpitations) occur and liaise with the client's cardiology team if needed.

Overview and structure
- Frequency: 3 gym sessions per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri) + 2 short active-recovery days (light walking/stretching) or supervised cardiac rehab-style aerobic on alternate days as tolerated. Two full rest days.
- Session split: Combination of aerobic (continuous and interval with conservative work:rest), resistance training (multi-joint and accessory), balance/mobility, and flexibility. Warm-up and cool-down every session.
- Progression: Gradual increase in volume and slight intensity while keeping HR below target. Use RPE and HR together. Aim to improve endurance, strength (functional), balance and body composition. No Valsalva — coach breathing: inhale during eccentric/relax, exhale during concentric/effort; avoid breath-holding.
- Monitoring: HR target <115 bpm; RPE 11–13. Keep sets relatively short (≤12 reps) and use controlled tempo. Avoid heavy loading and single-max tests. If HR nears 115 bpm, reduce pace/resistance or prolong rest.
- Nutrition & recovery: General healthy cardiac-focused guidelines provided below.

Baseline checks (before starting)
- Confirm clearance and any medication effects (beta-blockers lower max HR — adjust HR targets if applicable; if on beta-blocker, rely more on RPE and symptoms than raw HR).
- Baseline vitals resting and after light exertion (for trainer knowledge).
- Record baseline performance: 6‑minute walk distance or 10‑minute steady cycle as a submax aerobic baseline; 1–2 RM not required — estimate training loads by using a weight that elicits RPE 11–13 for 8–12 reps.

Warm-up and cool-down (every session)
- Warm-up 8–10 minutes: light cardio (treadmill walk, stationary bike, or rowing at easy pace) keeping HR well below target; dynamic mobility for shoulders, hips, spine; 1–2 light warm-up sets of first resistance exercise (very light).
- Cool-down 8–10 minutes: slow aerobic taper 5 min (walking or cycling), static stretching 3–5 min (hamstrings, calves, chest, lats, hip flexors), breathing/relaxation (paced diaphragmatic breathing).

Program phases
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation — low-to-moderate aerobic volume, light resistance focusing on movement patterns, balance, mobility.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build — increase aerobic duration and add light interval work still within HR limit; increase resistance volume and introduce slightly higher loading/complexity but keep repetitions moderate.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidate & maintain — further increase aerobic capacity, continued strength progression, more functional/compound movements, maintain safety constraints.

Weekly template (3 sessions per week)
- Session A: Aerobic-focused + full-body resistance (higher aerobic load)
- Session B: Strength-focus (resistance priority) + short aerobic warm-up and cool-down
- Session C: Mixed aerobic intervals + mobility/balance + lighter resistance

Detailed week-by-week plan

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4 (establish technique, cardiovascular confidence)
Goals: Establish routine, teach breathing, emphasize low-moderate steady-state aerobic and light resistance for 2–3 sets, 10–15 reps, RPE 11–13, HR <115 bpm.

Week 1
Session A
- Warm-up 8 min bike walk
- Aerobic: Treadmill walk 20 min at comfortable pace that keeps HR ~55–65% HRmax (target ~95–110 bpm), RPE 11–12
- Resistance circuit (2 rounds; rest 90–120s between rounds)
  - Seated chest press (machine) 2x12
  - Seated row (machine or cable) 2x12
  - Goblet squat (light kettlebell or dumbbell) 2x12 — depth as tolerated
  - Standing single-arm press (light dumbbell) 2x12 each
  - Bodyweight or assisted step-ups 2x10 each leg
- Core: Dead-bug 2x10 each side
- Cool-down 8 min walking + stretches

Session B
- Warm-up 8 min recumbent bike
- Resistance (2–3 sets; rest 90s)
  - Leg press 2x12
  - Lat pulldown 2x12
  - Dumbbell Romanian deadlift (light) 2x12
  - Dumbbell bench or incline press 2x12
  - Farmer carry (light dumbbells) 2 x 30–45s
- Balance/mobility: Single-leg stand 2x30s each with support as needed
- Cool-down

Session C
- Warm-up 8 min treadmill walk
- Aerobic intervals (conservative): 6 x (1.5 min faster walk / 2.5 min easy) — total ~24 min, keep HR below 115; RPE 12 on faster intervals
- Resistance (single set each, focus on quality)
  - Cable anti‑rotation press (Pallof) 2x10 each
  - Seated leg curl 2x12
  - Standing calf raise 2x12
- Mobility and breathing exercises

Weeks 2–4
- Gradually increase steady-state aerobic sessions from 20 → 30 min by week 4.
- Resistance: progress from 2 sets to 2–3 sets; maintain 10–15 reps. Slightly increase load only if client keeps HR/RPE targets and technique is good.
- Interval session: progress intervals to 8 x (1.5 min faster / 2 min easy) by week 4 if tolerated.
- Continue balance work; add light functional tasks (sit-to-stand for time).

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8 (build endurance and strength)
Goals: Increase aerobic duration and modestly increase resistance volume/complexity. Continue strict HR/RPE monitoring and breathing cues.

Week 5
Session A
- Warm-up 8 min bike + mobility
- Aerobic steady-state: 30 min treadmill or cycle at moderate pace (HR target mid to high of allowable but <115)
- Resistance circuit (3 rounds; rest 90s)
  - Machine leg press 3x10–12
  - Seated cable row 3x10–12
  - Dumbbell split squat (rear foot elevated or static lunge) 3x8–10 each leg (light)
  - Dumbbell overhead press seated 3x10
  - Hip bridge or glute bridge 3x12
- Core: Plank 2x20–40s (as tolerated)
- Cool-down

Session B
- Warm-up 8–10 min
- Resistance focused (3 sets; 60–90s rest)
  - Romanian deadlift with dumbbells 3x10
  - Incline machine press or dumbbell 3x10
  - Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up 3x10
  - Cable single-arm row 3x10 each
  - Standing unilateral carry 3 x 30–45s each side
- Balance/mobility: single-leg RDL support 2x8 each
- Cool-down

Session C
- Warm-up
- Aerobic intervals (conservative): 6–8 repeats of 2 min slightly brisk walk/1.5 min easy — HR should spike but remain <115; RPE 12–13 peak
- Light circuit: Bodyweight squat to box 2x12, bench-supported row 2x12, step-ups 2x10
- Mobility + breathing

Weeks 6–8
- Aerobic steady-state: increase to 35–40 min by week 8 (one session per week).
- Interval session: extend faster intervals up to 3 min with 2 min easy, limit to 6 repeats to control HR load.
- Resistance: progress load so sets are RPE 12–13 for 8–12 reps; maintain 3 sets for major lifts. Still avoid heavy single-rep efforts and Valsalva.
- Add low-impact cross-training option (elliptical, pool) once weekly if desired.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12 (consolidation, functional gains)
Goals: Improve sustained aerobic capacity and functional strength. Maintain safety limits. Emphasize pacing and day-to-day recovery.

Week 9
Session A
- Warm-up
- Aerobic steady-state: 40 min (treadmill incline walking or cycle) keeping HR <115. If on beta-blockers, follow RPE.
- Resistance circuit (3 rounds)
  - Leg press or goblet squat 3x10
  - Chest-supported row 3x10
  - Split squat or step-down 3x8–10 each leg
  - Seated overhead press 3x10
  - Farmer carry 3 x 45–60s
- Core: Side plank 2x20–30s each side
- Cool-down

Session B
- Warm-up
- Resistance emphasis (3–4 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Deadlift variation (trap bar light) 3x8–10 — controlled tempo; no heavy loads
  - Incline dumbbell press 3x10
  - Cable row 3x10
  - Single-arm dumbbell press 3x10
  - Hip hinge/glute medius work (clams, band walks) 3x12–15
- Balance: dynamic single-leg reaching 2x6 each
- Cool-down

Session C
- Warm-up
- Aerobic intervals (sustained but safe): 5–6 repeats of 3 min brisk / 2 min easy (total ~25–30 min). Keep HR cap.
- Light strength circuit (2 rounds): leg curl 2x12, standing row 2x12, calf raise 2x15
- Mobility and breathing

Weeks 10–12
- Slightly increase total aerobic weekly minutes (one session 45 min by week 12).
- Keep interval peaks controlled; avoid pushing HR to upper limits repeatedly.
- Strength: continue progression via small weight increases when RPE stays in 11–13. Emphasize functional lifts (squat, hinge, push, pull) with 3 sets of 8–12.
- End of week 12: retest functional measures — 6‑minute walk, timed sit-to-stand (as tolerated) to document improvement (no maximal testing).

Session examples (exercise details & cues)
- Tempo: controlled 2‑0‑2 (2s eccentric, no pause, 2s concentric) unless otherwise noted. Encourage exhale on exertion.
- Breathing cue: inhale during lowering/return phase; exhale during pushing/effort. Avoid breath-holding.
- Rest periods: 60–120s depending on session focus and HR recovery.
- Heart-rate pacing: after warm-up, check HR during steady-state; adjust speed/resistance to keep below 115. Use longer rests if HR remains high.

Avoidances and safety
- No Valsalva: continuously coach breathing and avoid maximal lifts.
- No maximal 1RM testing. Use submaximal loads with RPE guidance.
- If any angina, undue dyspnea, dizziness, palpitations, or syncope occur: stop exercise, sit/lie, monitor vitals, call emergency services per local protocol.
- Adjust target HR downward if clinician recommends or if on HR-lowering meds; rely more on RPE (11–13).

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Cardiac-healthy nutrition: emphasize Mediterranean-style eating — vegetables, fruit, whole grains, lean protein (fish, poultry, legumes), healthy fats (olive oil, nuts), limited saturated fat, processed foods, and reduced sodium if hypertension present.
- Protein: aim for ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day to support muscle maintenance (adjust with comorbidities/renal function).
- Hydration: regular, modest intake before/during/after sessions. Avoid large volumes that might stress circulation acutely.
- Sleep: target 7–8 hours per night to support recovery.
- Recovery days: light walking, gentle mobility, and structured breathing exercises. Encourage slow diaphragmatic breathing 5–10 minutes daily to support autonomic balance.
- Alcohol and caffeine: moderate alcohol reduction for cardiac benefit and avoid caffeine immediately before sessions if it causes palpitations.

Progress checks and adaptations
- Weekly check-ins on symptoms, medication effects, HR responses, sleep, appetite.
- Adjust volume/intensity if HR consistently approaches 115 bpm or RPE >13. If on beta-blockers or rhythm-control meds, set targets primarily by RPE and symptoms.
- If progress is good and cardiologist agrees, further gradual increases can be made beyond week 12.

Notes for the trainer
- Keep exercise logs: HR during session (rest, peak, post‑exercise minute 1), RPE, any symptoms.
- Educate client about warning signs and safe perceived effort.
- Use machines and supported movements early; progress to more free-weight and functional exercises as balance and confidence improve.
- Emphasize technique over load.

If you want, I can:
- Produce printable weekly sheets for the client with specific exercises and progression notes.
- Adjust HR targets based on medications (if you tell me beta-blocker status).
- Create modifications for joint issues (knees/hips/back) or diabetes if present.

Would you like printable, session-by-session sheets or to adjust for beta-blocker therapy?
